use_case: Electric load-forecasting model: hourly day-ahead and 7-day forecasts for the system and the 418 distribution substations, used for wholesale schedules, PPA dispatch, peak-day operating plans, and as an input to next-day TCC studies
business_owner: Director, Power Supply and Load Forecasting
vendor_or_model: In-house gradient-boosted regression ensemble on the Cloud provider B analytics platform, retrained monthly
data_categories: Historian load history (one-way export from the ADMS DMZ); AMI interval data aggregated to substation level (at least 100 meters per aggregate); weather forecasts; calendar; rooftop solar and EV estimates
affects_individuals: No (grid-level; indirect effect on customers through operating plans and rates)
human_in_the_loop: Power supply desk approves every day-ahead schedule; DCC and TCC shift supervisors approve peak-day plans; no automatic control action
applicable_laws: No AI-specific federal, Florida, or Georgia law identified for this use. Not a BES Cyber System (outside NERC CIP scope). Balancing Authority scheduling rules and PPA terms (contract). Guidance: NIST AI RMF 1.0
protected_characteristic_inputs: None (no individual data); substation-level effects assessed by neighborhood characteristics
bias_testing_status: Substation-level fairness test done for summer 2026 (two groups flagged; section 7.4)
monitoring: Daily error; monthly drift (manual today; automated alerts due 2026-12-31, POAM-029); quarterly substation fairness test
